_comment: Locked policy. Two parts: how a source motif becomes 20x20 art, and what may sit where on a given base. Both are data so the rules can be checked rather than remembered.

rules.when: the motif's target footprint is at least 3x3 cells
rules.why: measured A/B: at 3x3 and above a nearest-neighbour reduction and a hand redraw land within one cell of each other once the integration pass runs, so the cheaper path wins

rules.when: the target is smaller than 3x3, or carries a feature one cell wide
rules.why: below 3x3 point sampling starts MISSING the shape rather than simplifying it: the 2x3 gem lost a third of its cells to background sampling

rules.when: a resize drops cells the motif's identity depends on
rules.why: fidelity to the source is not the goal; recognisability at gameplay scale is

conversion.reject_if: it still reads as pasted, speckled or foreign at gameplay scale

soft_cap._comment: A cap is not a shallow fedora. Its zone vocabulary IS the policy: there is no band zone on a cap, so a hat band has nowhere to go and is banned by geometry rather than by a list.
soft_cap.banned_why: wide-brim and fedora dressing: a cap has no band to carry them and no brim to edge, and at this crown height they swamp the silhouette

cardinality.note: front_panel is its own occupancy region, so the existing one-motif-per-region rule already enforces this

soft_cap_front_emblem.zone: front_panel, derived from the widest CROWN row (never the visor row), inset 2 cells from the outline on each side and stopped 2 rows above the visor
soft_cap_front_emblem.seating: centred horizontally in the panel; vertically centred with the integer-division bias, which lands upper-middle
soft_cap_front_emblem.margin: at least one row of plain cloth between the emblem and the visor; an emblem may never touch or merge with the visor

directions.left/right: only where the foreshortened front crown is visible; the profile panel is 3 cells wide, so anything wider is dropped rather than squeezed — the compression is enforced by geometry, not by a per-view redraw
directions.back: none; the back view has no front_panel zone at all

soft_cap_front_emblem.enforced_by: cap_zones() in tools/author_base_assets.py and _placement() in v5/authored.py

cap_visor_grammar.derived_from: 29 cap-like hats in vanilla hats.png + the mod-author sheet, identified structurally (profile widest row projects off-centre forward over a shallow crown); see tools/analyze_cap_visor_corpus.py and output/softcap_foundation/visor_corpus.txt

width.front: NEVER wider than the crown. The canonical cluster (vanilla 16/18/43/77/94/102/109/113 and mod 44) is exactly 1.00 — a peak projects forward, and head-on you see it foreshortened, not spread. A front view wider than its crown reads as a brim.
width.profile: 1.10-1.56, median 1.25. The whole projection lives here.
width.note: This corrects an earlier guard that applied a single <=1.15 brim_ratio to every view; vanilla's own baseball caps measure 1.56 in profile.

value.rule: the visor breaks DARK from the crown above it
value.evidence: front: 17/29 darker, 2/29 lighter, median break -12; the canonical cluster runs -19 to -60. profile: 14/29 darker, 2/29 lighter.
value.why: the visor is a plane turning down and away from the light, so it takes the bottom of the ramp while the crown holds the top; that break, not the outline, is what makes a peak read at gameplay scale
value.range_use: vanilla 16 draws its crown at L 109-146 and its visor at L 23-41 on a 15-146 span — the crown lives at the TOP of the ramp, which is also what keeps the cap from reading as a dark blob

rows.front: 2 (median): a full-width dark band, then a narrower darkest edge

soft_cap.why: A procedurally authored cap that never read as naturally worn. Attempts: +1 cell per side, +1 crown row with a broadened apex, an aperture flare to head width, and a KEEP/HIDE/BALD hair-policy comparison. Metrics improved at each step; the in-game read did not.
soft_cap.superseded_by: source-derived constructions from `generator conent`, used as actual source pixels rather than redrawn
soft_cap.rule: do not modify this base again; do not regenerate a replacement for it

source_art_authority.rule: The source pixels are the construction authority.
do_not: average a source with other references
treat the source only as inspiration
workflow: identify only clearly separable reusable components
prove exact reconstruction of the original
use the real extracted pieces in the generator
source_art_authority.fallback: a component that cannot be separated without damaging the source is marked BASE-SPECIFIC or REFERENCE-ONLY, never regenerated
